situation: User asked why the built-in codex_apps MCP client failed to start while handshaking with https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/apps.
outcome: A reusable troubleshooting rule was extracted for remote MCP failures where the MCP client expects JSON/SSE but receives HTML challenge content or transport errors.
root_cause: Most likely proxy/VPN exit IP reputation or Codex GUI proxy inheritance caused chatgpt.com backend requests to receive a Cloudflare HTML challenge page; stale Codex auth remained a secondary possibility.
evidence: Shell curl HEAD reached the endpoint and returned 405 Allow: POST, proving basic reachability.
Unauthenticated initialize POST returned 401 Unauthorized, proving the endpoint requires auth rather than being absent.
Codex logs showed 403 Forbidden HTML challenge content and Unexpected content type text/html during MCP initialize.
The local config did not show a user-defined codex_apps MCP entry, indicating this was likely an internal Codex remote MCP rather than a malformed local config stanza.
solution: Switch proxy node and verify chatgpt.com browser login.
Set macOS GUI proxy environment with launchctl setenv for HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY, ALL_PROXY, and NO_PROXY.
Fully restart Codex so the GUI process inherits the proxy environment.
Run codex login or re-login in the app if auth remains suspect.
Avoid changing local MCP config unless logs prove a local config problem.
lesson: For remote MCP startup failures, first classify the response path as reachability, auth, challenge HTML, timeout, or local config before proposing fixes.

user_feedback.request: Persist the failure cause as a reusable rule
